title: Beauty and Personal Care Ecommerce Benchmarks in 2026
summary: Conversion rate, AOV and bounce rate data for the Beauty and Personal Care ecommerce category for 2026.
body_markdown:
## **TLDR — CVR Back Above 2025, AOV Up 7.8% Year-Over-Year**


The benchmarks:[3.15% median CVR](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-conversion-rate) ,[$274 median AOV](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-average-order-value) . The 25th–75th percentile AOV range is $138–$585. Beauty & Personal Care ranks second in CVR across all 10 published industries — and posted its second straight quarter of conversion gains in Q3, beating its seasonal baseline again.


Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date Ecommerce Benchmark Reports (January–September 2026), Beauty & Personal Care.


Beauty is one of the dataset’s most reliable converters. Loyal customers who already know a brand and its products tend to return and buy with less friction than shoppers in higher-consideration categories, and the 3.15% median reflects that dynamic at work. The first half of 2026 was soft — most months came in below their 2025 equivalents — but the category has since caught up. CVR rose 4.5% from Q2 to Q3 among stores active in both quarters, ahead of its +2.6% seasonal baseline, and every Q3 month ran above the same month of 2025. Bounce rate is the exception: it remains about 10 percentage points above 2025 levels.


On order value: the $274 median is the third-lowest of the 11 categories we track, above only Health & Wellness and Food & Beverage, with a P25-to-P75 spread of $138–$585. Year over year, same-store AOV is up 7.8% — the second-largest gain among reported categories — though it held flat from Q2 to Q3 (+0.6%). November 2025 remains the strongest single month in the trend window ($311).


> Beauty consistently ranks among the top-converting categories in the dataset. The 3.15% median reflects loyal-customer purchasing patterns that reliably outperform higher-consideration categories — and in Q3, conversion moved back above 2025 levels.


## **Conversion Rate Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date**


The median Beauty & Personal Care conversion rate from January through September 2026 was 3.15%, placing it second among the 10 published industries — just below Health & Wellness (3.22%).


n=803 active Shopify stores, January–September 2026. Stores with CVR below 0.1% or above 25% excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date CVR Benchmark Report.


The two top-converting categories — Health & Wellness and Beauty & Personal Care — share a defining characteristic: repeat purchasing. Customers who replenish supplements, skincare, or haircare products convert quickly because they have already done the consideration work. The session-to-order rate is high because the decision has essentially already been made before the session starts.


The 3.15% median sits well above the overall dataset median of 1.74% and roughly two and a half times the rate of the lower-converting categories like Autos & Vehicles (1.26%) and Sports & Outdoors (1.20%).


> Beauty & Personal Care’s bounce rate climbed from the 40–42% range in H1 2025 to 52–54% in Q3 2026. Loyal customers still convert — CVR is back above 2025 levels — but a larger share of inbound traffic is arriving and leaving without engaging. The trend data tells a more complete story than the headline alone.


## **CVR & Bounce Rate Trend — January 2025 through September 2026**


The chart below shows monthly median CVR and bounce rate for active Beauty & Personal Care stores in Shogun’s conversion tracking network. Twenty-one months of data makes the 2026 shift visible against a full year of 2025 baseline.


n=32–50 active stores per month. Each month measured on its own; CVR filter 0.1%–25% per site per month. Source: Shogun session and conversion tracking, Beauty & Personal Care.


CVR ran between 3.71% and 4.06% across H1 2025, and most of H1 2026 came in below that range — March 2026 (3.02%) was the low point. The November–December 2025 data stands out: CVR spiked to 5.15%–5.18% — the strongest consecutive months in the 21-month window — while bounce rate dropped to 39.2%–44.5%. In Beauty, the holiday period drove both higher conversion and higher basket sizes.


The bounce rate trajectory is the most significant signal in this data. Rates climbed from the 40–42% range across H1 2025 to 49–54% through 2026 — an increase of roughly 10 percentage points that has held for nine consecutive months. The loyal-customer base continues to convert; the shift points to a growing share of discovery or paid traffic that is not finding what it needs on the first page.


Within 2026, conversion has steadily recovered. CVR averaged around 3.32% across January–March, 3.82% across April–June and 3.84% across July–September — with July (4.13%), August (3.68%) and September (3.71%) all above their 2025 equivalents. That recovery is consistent with the category’s two consecutive same-store quarterly gains: +5.1% from Q1 to Q2 and +4.5% from Q2 to Q3.


## **Average Order Value Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date**


The 2026 year-to-date median AOV for Beauty & Personal Care was $274, based on period order totals across 341 qualifying stores. This data set is separate from the CVR cohort above — it covers full-store Shopify order data rather than Shogun-instrumented page sessions, and uses different qualifying criteria.


January–September 2026, n=341 stores with at least 375 orders; AOV above $5,000 excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date AOV Benchmark Report, Beauty & Personal Care.


## **AOV Trend — June 2025 through September 2026**


The chart below tracks monthly median AOV for Beauty & Personal Care stores, with each month measured on its own (290–327 stores per month). The trend starts in June 2025 because store coverage in the order data was much thinner before then.


n=290–327 stores per month; each month measured on its own (stores with at least 50 orders that month, AOV $1–$5,000). Source: Shogun AOV benchmark data, Beauty & Personal Care.


The most striking feature of the 16-month AOV trend is November 2025 ($311) — the high point of the window. November is a different demand environment for Beauty: gift sets, premium skincare routines, and limited-edition launches drive customers toward higher price points. The data shows Beauty’s holiday period lifting both conversion rate and basket size at the same time — a combination that doesn’t appear in all categories.


Outside November, the trend runs in a $251–$292 band, and 2026 has run slightly higher than 2025 on balance. May 2026 ($291) and September 2026 ($292) were the two strongest months outside the holiday spike, and September 2026 came in well above September 2025 ($263). Same-store AOV was flat from Q2 to Q3 (+0.6%).


On a matched same-store basis (n=270 stores active in both January–September 2025 and January–September 2026), median AOV grew from $266 to $287 — a +7.8% year-over-year increase. That figure is a better measure of per-store growth than the monthly trend, because it follows the same stores across both periods.


## **What CVR and AOV Are Saying Together**


Beauty & Personal Care’s 2026 story has turned from divergence toward recovery. Through the first half, CVR trailed 2025 while basket sizes grew. In Q3, conversion caught up: every Q3 month ran above its 2025 counterpart, and CVR rose for a second straight quarter (+4.5% from Q2 to Q3). AOV, measured on a matched same-store basis, is up 7.8% year over year for the 270 stores active in both periods, though it held flat from Q2 to Q3.


The bounce rate increase is the metric that still warrants the most attention. Beauty brands with strong repeat-purchase cohorts have a natural CVR floor — loyal customers will find the site and buy. But a bounce rate sitting roughly 10 percentage points above 2025 suggests that an increasing share of inbound sessions involves visitors who don’t recognize the brand or find the first page immediately relevant. Whether that traffic is from paid acquisition, discovery placements, or viral reach, it is arriving and leaving at a higher rate than in 2025.


The November–December 2025 data offers a reference point for what a high-conversion, high-AOV environment looks like in Beauty: CVR at 5.15%–5.18%, bounce rate at 39%–45%, AOV at $265–$311. Q3 2026 moved partway back toward that profile on conversion, but not on bounce rate, which remains well above holiday-period levels.


> If your CVR is above 3.15% but your bounce rate is also climbing, you are not alone — and your loyal core may be masking the growth challenge. The trend data here is a better diagnostic than the headline CVR alone.


## **A Note on Sub-Markets Within Beauty & Personal Care**


The $274 median is a meaningful benchmark — but the P25-to-P75 range tells an equally important story. The middle 50% of Beauty & Personal Care stores in this dataset have an AOV somewhere between $138 and $585. That $447 spread within a single category reflects the genuine breadth of what “Beauty & Personal Care” contains.


A brand selling everyday drugstore basics — lip balm, face wash, deodorant — operates on very different economics than one selling premium skincare routines, professional-grade tools, or luxury fragrance. Price point drives not just AOV but the entire purchase dynamic: replenishment of a $15 product happens differently from a considered purchase of a $200 serum. Conversion rates will follow the same pattern — the $138 P25 stores are likely replenishment-driven, the $585 P75 stores more deliberate.


The $274 median is your starting point, not your target. Your relevant benchmark is the sub-market you actually compete in — which may sit well above or below that headline figure depending on where your price points land.


The trend data — CVR back above 2025 levels in Q3, bounce rate still elevated, and AOV up 7.8% year over year on a matched cohort basis — applies at the category level. Sub-market dynamics may look different: luxury Beauty brands may show more AOV resilience, while mass-market brands may feel the traffic-quality shift more acutely.
